# `passportsim nfc_tap`

Tap the NFC card with a virtual phone: read or write NDEF, or send raw frames.

| MCP tool | Scenario step | macOS | Windows | Browser |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `passport_nfc_tap` | `nfc.tap` | yes | yes | yes |

## Synopsis

```text
passportsim nfc_tap [--dwell-ms <DWELL_MS>] [--instance <INSTANCE>] --json <@file|->
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Form | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dwell_ms` | `--dwell-ms <DWELL_MS>` | `integer` | no | Phone in field (300). |
| `instance` | `--instance <INSTANCE>` | `string` | no | Instance id. |
| `ops` | carried by `--json` | `array` | yes | - |

A nested object or array is passed as one JSON document with `--json @<file>` or `--json -`; it has no flag of its own.

## Errors

`E_USAGE` (1), `E_STATE` (2), `E_LEASE` (6), `E_SNAPSHOT` (15), `E_INTERNAL` (17). What each means: [errors.md](../errors.md).

## Examples

### Read the NDEF records

```sh
passportsim nfc_tap --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "op": "readNdef"
    }
  ]
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "op": "readNdef"
    }
  ]
}
'@ | passportsim nfc_tap --json -
```

### Write a URI record

```sh
passportsim nfc_tap --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "ndef": [
        {
          "type": "uri",
          "uri": "https://example.com/p"
        }
      ],
      "op": "writeNdef"
    }
  ]
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "ndef": [
        {
          "type": "uri",
          "uri": "https://example.com/p"
        }
      ],
      "op": "writeNdef"
    }
  ]
}
'@ | passportsim nfc_tap --json -
```

### Send GET_VERSION and READ 4 as raw frames

```sh
passportsim nfc_tap --json - <<'JSON'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "frames": [
        "60",
        "3004"
      ],
      "op": "raw"
    }
  ]
}
JSON
```

```powershell
@'
{
  "ops": [
    {
      "frames": [
        "60",
        "3004"
      ],
      "op": "raw"
    }
  ]
}
'@ | passportsim nfc_tap --json -
```
